title: Redwood Security & Privacy Review - Acme Health
topics: Prompt/content retention / training on customer data
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert
Redwood SE to schedule VPC technical deep dive and run benchmark on A100s
Customer to confirm required log retention window and residency region
Legal to review data processing addendum (DPA) and provide comments
action_items: Samira Patel: Share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate (due 2026-10-15)
Daniel Ortiz: Schedule VPC/private deployment deep dive and provide benchmark template (due 2026-10-19)
Renee Park: Send list of required contractual clauses for DPA and any PHI constraints (due 2026-10-18)
Omar Siddiq: Provide sample traffic profile and data residency requirement (due 2026-10-16)
summary: Acme Health ran a security and privacy review with Redwood to validate data handling controls for PII/PHI and confirm that Redwood does not train models on customer data. Main items: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/RBAC, audit logging & retention, KMS/encryption, EU data residency options, and prompt retention policies. Redwood confirmed hosted defaults retain prompts for 30 days for debugging but offered configurable retention and a no-retention option for enterprise/private deployments. Agreed next steps to exchange SOC reports and schedule technical VPC deep dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for making time, I'm Samira from Redwood. Today is a security and privacy review focused on data handling — happy to run through SOC2, SSO, KMS, and the prompt retention questions you sent.
[00:17] Laura Chen (Acme CISO): Thanks Samira. We have Renee, Miguel, and Omar on. Main asks: confirmation that Redwood doesn't train models on our data, how long prompts are retained, where data is stored for residency, and details around audit logs.
[00:35] Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE): Hey all, Daniel here. Quick note: I'll cover technical architecture, encryption, K M S details, and options for private deployments.
[00:48] Miguel Alvarez (Lead ML Eng): Quick clarifying q — when you say "no training on customer data" is that a legal promise or technical isolation? Our regulators require an explicit guarantee for PHI.
[01:02] Samira: Good q. Short answer: we do not use customer prompts or content to train or fine-tune our models. Longer: for hosted accounts we have a policy and contractual language in the DPA that prohibits training on customer data, and for Dedicated/Private customers, data stays in customer-controlled environments. We can provide the exact DPA language.
[01:28] Renee Park (Privacy Counsel): We need to see that in writing and ideally have a log of data flows. Also, does Redwood keep copies of prompts in any analytics or debugging caches?
[01:42] Daniel: By default, our hosted API keeps request/response logs for troubleshooting and abuse detection. Default retention is 30 days for logs and traces, but it's configurable. For enterprise customers we offer options: extended retention, shorter retention, or zero retention where logs are not persisted beyond ephemeral processing. For Dedicated and Private deployments you control storage and can set policies to disable logging.
[02:10] Omar Siddiq (Cloud Architect): When you say "disable logging" — does that mean no audit logs at all? We do need auditability for compliance.
[02:20] Daniel: Good point — we differentiate between two things: (1) telemetry/debug logs used by support and (2) audit logs required for compliance. Audit logs (auth events, API call metadata, admin changes) can be routed to customer-controlled sinks — e.g., shipped to your cloud logging (CloudWatch/Stackdriver) or to a SIEM. So you can have audit trails without Redwood retaining payload content.
[02:46] Laura: Can you confirm encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS integration? We use a managed HSM and need CKA-level control.
[02:55] Daniel: All data in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we use envelope encryption: data is encrypted with service keys that are wrapped by a customer-managed K M S key for Dedicated and Private customers. For hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed KMS by default but can integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated/private. We also support HSM-backed keys through major cloud KMS providers.
[03:21] Miguel: How do you handle the KV cache and longer context? Is anything persisted that could be used for training?
[03:31] Daniel: The KV cache is in-memory per-request in our serving tier; we persist checkpoints only for session resumption in Dedicated/private when configured, but those are stored encrypted and scoped to the tenant. We do not extract these for training.
[03:45] Renee: SOC 2 Type II evidence — can we get the report and a summary of scope?
[03:51] Samira: Yes — action: I'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert. The scope includes our control plane, hosted API, and production serving runtime; we'll include the date range and any exclusions.
[04:06] Laura: Data residency — we need EU-only processing and storage for certain datasets. Is that supported?
[04:12] Daniel: Yep. We offer region pinning for data and serving. For hosted, we have EU regions and can ensure data and logs remain within EU. For Dedicated/private we can deploy entirely in your VPC/region. Note there may be latency differences depending on model placement.
[04:30] Miguel: About training again — we get auditors asking: do you ever snapshot customer traffic and send to annotation or third-party vendors?
[04:39] Samira: We do not send customer prompts or outputs to third-party annotators. We use internal telemetry for product improvement, but that is aggregated and does not include customer content. For any research usage we have an explicit opt-in process.
[04:55] Omar: What's the retention for audit logs if we route them to your managed service?
[05:01] Daniel: If routed to Redwood-managed storage default is 1 year for audit logs, but most enterprise customers route to their own SIEM and control retention. We can set retention by log type.
[05:12] Renee: PHI — if our data includes PHI, are you willing to sign a BA A?
[05:17] Samira: Redwood is open to BAAs for customers processing PHI. We have customers with healthcare workloads and our legal team will follow the BAA template. We'll include clauses on breach notification, encryption, and subprocessors.
[05:30] Laura: SSO and RBAC — we need SAML with SCIM provisioning and granular RBAC tied to AD groups.
[05:38] Maya Lin (Redwood CSM): We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning. Our RBAC is role-based with custom roles possible for Dedicated accounts; group sync is available for SSO providers so you can map AD groups to roles.
[05:55] Laura: Is there audit trail for admin role changes?
[05:58] Daniel: Yes, admin changes are recorded in audit logs with who/when via SSO identity. Those can be exported and sent to your SIEM.
[06:10] Miguel: Any support for token policy and ephemeral keys — we prefer short-lived tokens for API access.
[06:16] Daniel: We support short-lived tokens and can integrate with your STS to mint temporary credentials. For Dedicated deployments we can integrate with your identity provider for token exchange.
[06:28] Laura: Regarding data deletion — if we request deletion, how fast is that enforced? Are there backups that retain data longer?
[06:36] Samira: We have documented data deletion workflows. For hosted accounts, deletion requests remove active data within 48 hours, and backups are purged within 30-90 days depending on the backup schedule; we can shorten that for enterprise contracts. For Dedicated/private you control backup lifecycle. We'll include the deletion SLA in the DPA.
[06:58] Renee: Can you show the exact DPA excerpt that says "no training on customer data"? Auditors expect precise wording.
[07:06] Samira: Absolutely — I'll include the exact DPA excerpt. The clause states that Redwood will not use customer content to train models, and will not share content with third-party annotators, except as explicitly agreed.
[07:18] Miguel: About telemetry — do you collect embeddings or derived features? Could those be considered PII?
[07:26] Daniel: We may collect derived telemetry like token counts, latencies, and anonymized usage metrics. We do not persist raw prompts unless retention is enabled. If you have specific concerns about embeddings, we can disable embedding storage and route them to your tenant-only stores.
[07:41] Laura: Pen tests — do you publish recent penetration test results or just attestations?
[07:47] Samira: We have third-party pen test attestations and summaries; we can provide an executive summary and redacted report under NDA.
[07:58] Omar: For EU residency, are keys stored in-region if using customer-managed KMS?
[08:03] Daniel: Yes — if you supply a KMS key in the EU region, the wrapped keys and key material stay in-region per cloud provider guarantees.
[08:13] Laura: Any limitations for private clusters with respect to model updates or security patches? We want security patch SLAs.
[08:20] Daniel: For Dedicated we run coordinated patch windows; we publish maintenance schedules and offer emergency patching. For Private on-prem we provide upgrade bundles and can assist with staging; patch SLA can be included in enterprise contracts.
[08:36] Renee: How granular can we get with logging? We want to log both API events and admin console activity.
[08:43] Daniel: Both are available. API events include request metadata (no payload if you choose), response codes, latency. Console events include admin logins, role assignments, and config changes.
[08:58] Samira: I'll pause here and ask if we've hit your main questions or if we should deep dive on anything.
[09:04] Laura: Good so far — Miguel, any technical follow-ups?
[09:07] Miguel: Yes, I'd like the SE to run a quick benchmark with our sample workload and validate that KV cache cleanup doesn't leak across tenants. Also want to confirm model variant fallbacks in Dedicated mode.
[09:19] Daniel: We can run a benchmark. For KV cache isolation, our runtime enforces tenant boundaries and we have tests. For fallbacks, we have compatible model families deployed; Dedicated can be configured to prefer local variants with fallback to cloud-hosted variants only under policy you set.
[09:38] Laura: Anything about insurance or cyber liability?
[09:41] Samira: We carry cyber insurance; details are in the security pack. We'll include limits and insurer name.
[09:48] Renee: On training again, is there any situation where de-identified customer data could be used for research?
[09:55] Samira: Only with explicit opt-in and after de-identification review by our privacy team. By default no.
[10:03] Miguel: One more: does Redwood provide the ability to scrub PII from prompts automatically?
[10:09] Daniel: We offer pre-built content filters and a PII redaction API you can run client-side before sending, or enable server-side redaction with the caveat that server-side redaction might involve temporary processing but not training. For max assurance many customers run redaction client-side or in their VPC.
[10:29] Laura: Ok we need the SOC report, DPA excerpt, and a bench test. Let's recap the next steps.
[10:36] Samira: Agreed. Recap: we will send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, the DPA excerpt with the training prohibition, and Daniel will schedule a technical deep dive and benchmark. Renee will provide contract asks and Omar will provide traffic profile.
[10:51] Miguel: Timeline: we'd like to have the docs by Oct 15 and the deep dive week of Oct 19.
[10:58] Samira: That works for us.
[11:00] Maya: I'm adding notes to the account and will set up the calendar invites.
[11:04] Laura: Thanks all. End of call.
[11:08] (call ends)
